label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, secret-rotation, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy webhook-receiver: WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION v2 -> v1); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 156 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: webhook-receiver was redeployed at 19:09:21Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The provider is still signing webhooks with the secret the receiver used before, so the receiver now refuses them with 400 'bad signature' (signature mismatch). Refused webhooks are never acknowledged, and their events never reach Kafka. The provider keeps retrying them, so the received rate climbs while the 200s fade out. The unacknowledged count grows (156 at the alert, 219 at c1), the books cannot settle up to the cutoff, and BooksBehindProvider fires. The trailing 200s are most likely requests already in flight or counted in the rate window before the switch. Open questions: I did not confirm which secret version the receiver ran before (the deploy log should hold it, and the rollback uses it). I also did not confirm that the provider expects v1, rather than the v2 secret being loaded wrong.

evidence.shows: The money check could not run: after 30 s, 219 webhooks were still not acknowledged by our receiver, up from 156 at the alert. The symptom is confirmed and growing.
webhook-receiver was redeployed at 19:09:21Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, about 50 s before the alert. All other services were created together at 19:07:54Z with normal settings.
Webhooks received climb from about 2/s to about 20/s after 19:09:30, which is the provider's retry storm.
400s on /webhooks/provider start at 19:09:50, right after the deploy, and reach about 21/s, while 200s fall toward 0.8/s.
webhook-receiver logs many WARNING 'webhook refused: bad signature' lines with reason 'signature mismatch'.
The ERROR/WARN filter found nothing because the receiver logs at level WARNING, not WARN. This explains why the earlier log search came back empty.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to the settings it ran before the 19:09:21Z deploy, so it verifies with the secret version the provider signs with. The provider's retries will then be acknowledged, and their events will flow to Kafka and both consumers. Re-run the money check to confirm the books settle. Rotate to v2 only once the provider signs with v2, or once the receiver accepts both versions during the switch.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Only webhook-receiver is recreated, so webhook intake pauses briefly. The provider keeps retrying unacknowledged webhooks, so nothing is lost. When intake resumes, a burst of retried webhooks will arrive. The consumers are idempotent (ledger: idempotent, confirmer: by_our_id), so duplicates should not double-book. If the old secret was retired on purpose, for example because it was compromised, the rollback re-accepts it.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the 400s continue or get worse after the rollback, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, then check which secret the provider actually signs with before changing anything else.
